scope: aw_i2c_probe publication of richtap_misc and g_aw_haptic

observations: misc_open invokes the driver open callback while holding misc_mtx
misc_deregister removes the list entry and device node, then unlocks; it has no wait for already-open files
remap_pfn_range_internal marks mappings VM_IO and VM_PFNMAP
the target source describes VM_PFNMAP entries as raw PFN mappings without an associated struct page

locations: no cancellation call for state+0x668 in this function
state+0x448 queue pointer and state+0x668 work item at 0xb5d4-0xb5e0
load backing pointer from state+0x610 at 0xbb70
no per-device reference release in this function
stock worker callback for state+0x668; candidate source derives the state base as work-0x668 and reads state operations

findings.title: misc-device publication precedes state-pointer publication
findings.impact: An open callback can successfully store a null first-probe global or stale state pointer in file->private_data before the probe stores the new device pointer.

findings.title: open file descriptors can outlive resource teardown
findings.impact: An already-open file can race removal or invoke the ioctl after resources are released; ioctl 0x5209 accesses the freed buffer at state+0x608.

findings.title: Richtap stop work at state+0x668 is not canceled by aw_remove
findings.impact: ioctl 0x5212 queues a worker whose state base is derived from the embedded work address; removal has no matching cancel_work_sync for this item and does not close admission before resource teardown.

findings.title: mapped PFNs are released while userspace mappings may persist
findings.impact: The 0x4000-byte VM_PFNMAP can retain the physical mapping after free_pages returns its backing pages to the allocator; allocator reuse and user-visible effect were not exercised.

limits: This report records stock behavior and the current stock-matching candidate; it is not a hardware test.
The target misc.c and mm/memory.c were read from the pinned Docker kernel-source volume and their hashes are recorded above.
No source reconstruction files were changed and no Docker rebuild was run for this read-only review.
No CVE, exploitability, or deterministic crash claim is made.
The absence of destroy_workqueue in aw_remove is recorded as an open release surface, not independently labeled a leak.
hardening_follow_up: Publish initialized per-device state before misc_register and handle a failed registration.
Close new admission during removal and guard each file operation with a per-device lifetime reference and dying state.
Drain both Richtap work items at offsets +0x648 and +0x668 before releasing state or destroying the queue.
Tie page allocation lifetime to VMA references or use a mapping interface that retains page references.
Keep hardening changes separately identified from stock-equivalent reconstruction and revalidate them in the canonical Docker build.
